intent: The heading that names a sheet's panel.
typical_uses: The panel's heading, inside its SheetHeader

dont_use_when.situation: A heading for a section inside the panel's body

instead.target: a plain heading element (h3 and below)
instead.note: Only one SheetTitle names the panel; a section heading is ordinary content.

dont_use_when.situation: The heading of a centered dialog

invariants.text: SheetTitle renders an h2 set in the heading-2 type ramp with no margin.

anti_patterns.dont: Render a second SheetTitle in the same panel
anti_patterns.do_instead: Keep one SheetTitle per sheet and use plain headings for any subheadings; only one title can name the panel

render.states: render replaces the rendered element with one the caller supplies
render.because: Base UI's render prop takes an element or a function of the title's state, so its type is a union of a React element and a callback - the compiler emits one JSON type per property; the primitive passes an empty state object.

style.states: style accepts a function as well as a plain style object; the primitive passes that function an empty state object
style.because: Base UI widens React's `CSSProperties` to `CSSProperties | ((state) => CSSProperties)`, and the title's state carries no fields. The compiler emits one JSON type per property, so nothing is asserted; the kit's own styling goes through sheet.module.css, not through this.

bad.title: A plain heading in place of SheetTitle
bad.why: A plain heading carries no id the primitive knows about, so the panel gets no `aria-labelledby` and a screen reader announces an unnamed dialog.

render.description: TS: ReactElement<unknown, string | JSXElementConstructor<any>> | ComponentRenderFn<HTMLProps, DialogTitleState> | undefined. The compiler emits one JSON type per property; this type is left to tsc. render replaces the rendered element with one the caller supplies.
